Hi Liam — copying the technical details here and attaching our KMS Q&A workbook. High-level answers below; happy to walk through on the call.

Q: Encryption at-rest?
A: All hosted Redwood data is encrypted at-rest with AES-256 using per-tenant keys. For hosted customers we use envelope encryption; we store a data key encrypted by a KMS-managed key.

Q: In-transit?
A: All service-to-service and client connections use TLS 1.3 with strong ciphers; mutual TLS available for private deployments if required by policy.

Q: Customer-managed keys / BYOK?
A: Supported. Options: 
  - Redwood-managed KMS (default): AWS KMS (multi-region CMKs) — we manage rotation and access.
  - Customer-managed AWS KMS: Customer provides CMK with IAM policies that allow Redwood to use the key to encrypt/decrypt data-encryption keys. We support key policies and grants workflows.
  - HSM / On-prem KMS: For Private deployments we can integrate with customer HSMs (PKCS#11) or third-party key brokers; wrapping/unwrapping can be done in-customer scope so root keys never leave customer HSM.

Q: HSM-backed keys / FIPS?
A: We support HSM-backed key material for customers that require FIPS 140-2/3 validation; we can provide architecture diagrams during the SE call.

Q: Key rotation and access controls?
A: Rotation supported via standard KMS key rotation and a key versioning scheme in our runtime. We log all KMS operations to audit trails and can export logs to your SIEM (CloudTrail or syslog for private deployments).

Q: SOC 2 status?
A: Redwood is currently in progress on SOC 2 Type II for our inference platform; we are able to provide SOC 2 readiness artifacts and our security overview while the Type II report is finalized. See attached Redwood_Security_Overview.pdf and KMS_Q_and_A.xlsx.

Next steps we propose:

2) Schedule the technical deep-dive: Thu 3/5 10:00 PT works for us; please confirm attendees.
3) We can start a DPA/DocuSign flow once you confirm legal contacts and provide desired SLA items.
